answer: Require each agent to complete a fresh sequential verifiable-delay puzzle seeded by its submission before it can publish. The puzzle cannot be parallelized, so one machine cannot fake a whole orchard of identities at once; each new vertex in the trust graph must first emit this costly timing signal. An attacker who wants a thousand fake agents must pay a thousand sequential delays plus a fee that rises quadratically with submissions per epoch, while an honest agent pays only once. Forging scale becomes slower and pricier than honest participation.
